edge_players.edge_sentence: Dobbins is a 35-carry, 121-yard back (3.46 YPC, about 40 yards a game) running into an SF defense that has allowed 3.79 YPC and only 3 runs of 10+, and 59.5 is nearly 20 yards above that role.
edge_players.must_be_true: He keeps the lead-back share near 11-14 carries, SF's run wall shows up, and there is no long breakaway of the kind SF has barely allowed.
edge_players.kills_it: DEN controls the game and feeds him 18+ carries, or one 20-plus run SF has not been giving up, and he clears 59.5 without a role change visible in this pack.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Black already has 25 carries for 107 yards (4.28 YPC, about 36 a game) next to CMC, and he is running at a DEN defense that has allowed 5.30 YPC and 9 runs of 10+, against a 21-yard line well under that role.
edge_players.must_be_true: The complementary share holds near 6-9 carries and DEN's run defense stays as soft as the 5.30 YPC and 9 explosive-run sample.
edge_players.kills_it: CMC monopolizes carries in a competitive game, or the 25 carries were concentrated in one of three weeks and week 4 is a decoy role — splits and the injury report are not in the pack.

data_check.notes: No projection, sim median, or Pinnacle no-vig is in the pack, so this check is qualitative. Dobbins: 11.7 carries times SF's 3.79 YPC allowed is about 44 yards, and his own L3 rate is 40.3, both well under 59.5 — agrees with the under. Black: L3 35.7 rush yards vs a 21 line, with DEN allowing 5.30 YPC — agrees with the over. No model number contradicts either read, and no leg was stamped above 70% because no model was run. Black's price is +nan, so there is nothing sharp to size. CMC rush over 65.5 was dropped: 11.7 times 5.30 is about 62, still short of 65.5, and L3 form of 55 disagrees with that lean, so step 8 drops it rather than flags it.

market_rung_price: jkdobbins rushyds under 59.5 at -114, a role-and-wall under, not a short-priced alt. kaelonblack rushyds over 21 is listed at +nan, so the rung cannot be priced or sized from the pack until a real number is posted. No passing yards, TDs, or receptions.
pre_mortem: Monday case against the Dobbins under: Denver stayed neutral, the 35 carries hide an uptrend, he got 16 carries, and one 15-yard gain SF has rarely allowed pushed him to 61-70, so 59.5 was the right number. Against the Black over: CMC took 20 carries, Black was a 4-carry changeup and finished at 12, and the 21-yard line was the market correctly fading a role that only showed up when SF was already ahead. The Dobbins counter still loses to 11.7 carries times a 3.79 YPC wall. The Black counter is the stronger of the two, which is why that leg stays a lean, but 25 carries in three games is too much usage to call the counter the better read. Weather, inactives, and a snap limit are unchecked ways both legs die.
slip_story: One story: the run environment is split. SF can run on DEN (5.30 YPC, 9 runs of 10+) and DEN cannot run through SF (3.79 YPC, 3 runs of 10+). Dobbins under 59.5 and Black over 21 win together if SF is level or ahead and both backfields keep their L3 shares; they lose together if DEN jumps ahead and flips the run script. Do not add a DEN pass over or a total — spread and total were not saved, and a trailing-DEN pass over needs the opposite script. CMC rush over 65.5 is the same story at the wrong rung (form 55, matchup math about 62). No second market on either player.
